name: Nashitsubo no gonin (Minamoto no Shitagō et al.)
bio: The Five Men of the Pear Pavilion (Nashitsubo no gonin) were the court poets Minamoto no Shitagō, Ōnakatomi no Yoshinobu, Kiyohara no Motosuke, Sakanoue no Mochiki and Ki no Tokibumi. Around 951 Emperor Murakami set them up in the Pear Pavilion (Nashitsubo) of the imperial palace to read the old poems and to compile the second imperial anthology of waka.

They are the compilers of the Gosen wakashū (Later Collection of Japanese Poems), finished by about 957, which continues the Kokin wakashū. Its 1,425 poems stand in twenty books of seasons, love, miscellany, parting and travel, congratulation and grief. This page carries the work itself; the individual poems are credited to their many authors only in the source, not here.
